summary: HTTP/2 SETTINGS frame reordering from a client library causing stream-reset surge and upstream runtime restarts
description: Issue summary: Customers observed a rapid spike in 5xx responses (~40% elevated) for a subset of dedicated tenants. Impact: streaming sessions aborted with HTTP/2 RST_STREAM and many short-lived 502/503 responses; several runtime pods restarted from watchdog OOMs. Environment: prod-us-east-1, dedicated capacity pool serving NoteScale Analytics traffic. Time window: 2026-03-12 18:22 - ongoing (investigation active).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Client library (NoteScale SDK v2.1.3) opens multiplexed HTTP/2 connections to api-gateway and sends a rapid SETTINGS update sequence during connection spin-up.
2) SETTINGS frames arrive out-of-order (duplicate max_concurrent_streams updates) followed immediately by a burst of new stream initiations (many short-lived streaming sessions + embedding uploads).

3) api-gateway forwards to HTTP/2 proxy which attempted to reconcile the mismatched SETTINGS and temporarily rejected new streams, returning RST_STREAM to clients and queuing accept backpressure to upstream runtimes.
4) Upstream runtimes experienced accept-queue growth, large KV cache churn, and then memory pressure leading to OOM watchdog restarts under sustained ~600 rps burst.
Note: reproducible only with client behavior that emits duplicate/reordered SETTINGS during rapid connection creation.
observed_behavior: Rapid increase in 502/503 responses for streaming endpoints and short-lived 5xx spikes on generation endpoints. Runtime pods showed short-lived high RSS followed by SIGKILL (OOM). APIGW logs show repeated HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames and downstream RST_STREAMs. Traces show half-closed streams and accept-queue growth on proxies.
expected_behavior: HTTP/2 SETTINGS updates should be handled idempotently with no cascade of stream resets; the gateway/proxy should apply sensible backpressure without causing upstream OOMs or client-visible 5xx spikes.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 18:30 - Initial triage: Support received customer report; elevated 5xx correlated to NoteScale's tenant id and to a narrow time window. Alerting flagged runtime restarts and proxy accept-queue growth.
2026-03-12 18:42 - SRE reproduced malformed sequence using a synthetic client that replays SETTINGS frames and observed identical accept-queue behavior on staging proxys.

2026-03-12 19:05 - Hypothesis: client library aggressively reconfigures SETTINGS during connection warmup and our proxy's SETTINGS handling path has a bug that causes transient refusal of new streams instead of graceful negotiation.

2026-03-12 19:25 - Correlation found between high concurrent short-stream churn (keepalive + half-closed) and KV cache invalidations on runtime; frequent cold allocations led to memory fragmentation and watchdog OOMs.

2026-03-13 08:10 - Engineering acked root cause: http2 library path in proxy (nghttp2 wrapper) did not dedupe or coalesce duplicate SETTINGS in certain race windows, causing over-eager stream rejection and backpressure amplification.

short_term_mitigation: 1) Applied tenant-scoped new-connection rate limit at edge for NoteScale to reduce SETTINGS churn. 2) Requested customer to delay nightly batch that creates high connection churn or downgrade SDK to prior version. 3) Increased proxy accept-queue soft-limit temporarily to avoid immediate rejects.
resolution: Partial mitigation in place; root cause patch merged and staged. Canary rollout scheduled. Customer-facing errors reduced after edge throttling. Awaiting successful canary then full rollout.
resolution_details: Engineers fixed SETTINGS handling in the http2 wrapper: dedupe/coalesce SETTINGS updates and ensure atomic negotiation with stream creation. Proxy patch: grace-period for in-flight stream ops while SETTINGS applied. Runtime memory-pressure mitigations: reduce aggressive prefetch and tuned KV cache GC on canary to avoid immediate OOM during residual churn.
follow_up_actions: 1) Post-deploy validation: monitor 1hr, 6hr, 24hr windows for NoteScale tenant and other customers for SETTINGS-related errors.
2) Run targeted chaos test: simulate duplicate SETTINGS and high short-stream churn in staging (owner: SRE).
3) Improve telemetry: add a SETTINGS-frame counter metric on APIGW and proxy and an alert for repeated duplicate SETTINGS per connection.
4) Documentation: update client SDK guidance to avoid aggressive SETTINGS changes during bulk connection warmup; coordinate with NoteScale to publish recommended SDK configuration.
5) Postmortem: create incident postmortem with timeline and share with product & SDK teams (owner: Support/Eng).
